topic: The Engine of AI: Cost Functions and Gradient Descent
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Data Science beginners)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Mental Model (0:30)
lecture_lines: Neural networks map inputs to outputs.
Learning adjusts parameters to minimize errors.
Think of a robot throwing a ball.
animations: Add an arrow from 'Input' to 'Processing' in #FFFF00.
Highlight 'Processing' box with a glowing #00FF00 outline.

sections.title: Measuring Failure: The Cost Function (1:00)
lecture_lines: High cost means the guess is wrong.
animations: Draw a parabola representing the error landscape in #FFFFFF.
Place a point on the parabola at a high value in #FF0000.

sections.title: The Landscape: Visualization of Cost (1:00)
lecture_lines: Imagine cost as a mountain range.
The lowest valley represents minimum error.
Weights define our position on the landscape.
animations: Generate a 3D-like surface graph using lines in #FFFFFF.
Show contour lines to represent flat regions of the landscape.

sections.title: Descending: The Gradient Descent Algorithm (1:30)
lecture_lines: Gradient descent calculates the steepest downward slope.
A large learning rate risks overshooting.
animations: Draw a steep arrow representing the 'Negative Gradient' in #FF0000.
Show a step 's' moving the current point along the gradient.
Repeat step movement five times to simulate iterative descent.

sections.title: Integration & Conclusion (1:00)
lecture_lines: The loop is: predict, measure, update.
We repeat this to train the network.
animations: Display a summary list of 5 steps in #FFFFFF.
Boldly animate the transition from 'Initial State' to 'Optimized'.
Flash all elements in sequence to reinforce the loop.
